title: 前CIA分析师：出国别聊其他美国人，你清楚对方在向谁汇报吗？
speaker: Peter Mattis

segments.en: They should be, well, they shouldn't, I mean, first, this doesn't necessarily happen in China, correct? This can happen in Singapore, it could happen in Hong Kong, it could happen
segments.zh: 首先，这不一定发生在中国，对吧？可能在新加坡，可能在香港，也可能在

segments.en: Kuala Lumpur, it could happen in Brussels or Paris, right? It doesn't matter where it is.
segments.zh: 吉隆坡，可能在布鲁塞尔或巴黎，对吧？地点并不重要。

segments.en: I think the first is, you know, know what your red lines are. What are the things that can't be talked about? Second, know what your value is, particularly from a political side, right? In one sense,
segments.zh: 我认为首先，要清楚你的红线是什么。哪些话题不能谈？其次，要清楚你的价值，尤其是从政治角度，对吧？某种意义上，

segments.en: you could see that there's very clearly a benefit to the Chinese state in this operation, getting access to the chips, but there's also access to political intelligence, conceivably the
segments.zh: 你可以看到，中国在这项行动中明显有好处，能获取芯片，但也可能获取政治情报， conceivably

segments.en: ability to influence US policy, right? These things all exist together, and people should be cognizant of who is in their political circle, who are they, who is in their social circle, right? What is it
segments.zh: 影响美国政策的能力，对吧？这些因素同时存在，人们应该意识到谁在自己的政治圈子里，他们是谁，谁在自己的社交圈子里，对吧？我该谈论什么？

segments.en: that I should be talking about? I think a good rule, though, is if you're traveling abroad as an American, don't talk about other Americans if you can possibly help because you don't necessarily
segments.zh: 我认为一个好规则是，如果你是美国人出国旅行，尽可能不要谈论其他美国人，因为你不一定

segments.en: know who you're dealing with, and you don't know who they're reporting to. There's this meme that's been going around, yes, I'm going there, and it's how to tell if your girlfriend is a Chinese spy,
segments.zh: 知道你在和谁打交道，也不知道他们向谁汇报。有个流传的梗，是的，我要说这个，如何判断你的女朋友是不是中国间谍，

segments.en: and it's a joke, and it's tongue-in-cheek, and it's, are you in tech? Yes, is she more attractive than you? Yes, spy, it's ridiculous, but there has to be some sort of briefings, op-sec. I've
segments.zh: 这是个玩笑，半开玩笑的，比如：你在科技行业吗？是的，她比你更有吸引力吗？是的，间谍。这很荒谬，但必须有某种简报、行动安全。我

segments.en: heard of people in high intelligence jobs being warned about this exact thing, being warned about young attractive women approaching them for information. I've seen it happen. I've been with an
segments.zh: 听说从事高情报工作的人被警告过这一点，被警告有年轻有吸引力的女性接近他们获取信息。我见过这种情况。我曾和一位

segments.en: intelligence officer at a conference when a young woman went up and tried to get that person's information, and that intelligence officer knew immediately what it was, and shut it down.
segments.zh: 情报官员在会议上，一位年轻女性上前试图获取那人的信息，那位情报官员立刻知道是怎么回事，并制止了。
